meta.title: Multiscale Organization of Neural Networks in a 3D Bioprinted Matrix.

extracted_by: seed: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Rat embryonic cortical neurons were printed in GelMA at cortex-like density to form '3D neuMatrix' with long-range axon connections. The model was used to mimic ischemic stroke.

formulations.review_notes: Viability is reported as relative ATP (%) rather than percent live cells, so viability_percent is left null.
formulations.name: GelMA30 6% (3D neuMatrix)
formulations.key_outcome: Printed neurons formed 3D networks with local and long-range functional axon connections; used as an ischemic stroke model.

evidence.quote: to a final concentration of 1.5×107 cells mL−1 in 6% (w/v) GelMA30
we have chosen a 21G nozzle with an inner diameter of 510 µm to reduce the shear force
The bioprinting process utilized an extrusion‐based bioprinter (SUNP BIOTECH)
